source.title: Fisher Rank Inflation: A Spectral Signature of Memorization under Label Noise

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures memorization under label corruption alongside clean test performance, but its Fisher-spectrum measurements do not test the claim versions about random-label capacity, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, regularization, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports training accuracy on corrupted labels and clean test-accuracy trajectories, but does not report numerical test-accuracy values in the supplied text. Fisher-rank results measure a different property from the measures named in the versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorization under partial label corruption and its Fisher-spectrum signature, but none of V1–V8's specified comparisons. V1 requires a random-label versus natural-label comparison, including chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels; the corruption sweep stops at 60%. Fisher effective rank is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness, and deleting gradients at a fixed checkpoint is not V8's removal-and-retraining intervention.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify Fisher Rank Inflation as an architecture-dependent spectral signature of memorization under synthetic and human label noise, supported by corrupted-example enrichment and increasing peak rank with corruption severity. They explicitly qualify the timing analysis as retrospective and do not establish a universal predictor of overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains on partially corrupted labels and analyzes centered last-layer gradient spectra; it does not reproduce the listed interventions or generalization measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Corruption severity changes peak Fisher effective rank and clean test accuracy; architecture changes the strength of the attribution signal and the lead-time pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 approaches near-perfect provided-label training accuracy at corruption rates of 20–60%, while higher corruption produces lower clean test accuracy. Exact accuracy values are not readable from the supplied figure text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks can fit partially corrupted training labels while clean generalization deteriorates with increasing corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: Peak centered last-layer Fisher effective rank increases from 28.88 ± 1.95 without corruption to 97.09 ± 1.78 at 60% corruption, and exhibits an inflation–collapse trajectory during memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorization under label noise is accompanied by transient expansion of the last-layer gradient spectrum.

fits_no_version.finding: At peak-rank checkpoints, corrupted examples constitute 69.2–96.2% of the top-100 rank contributors under synthetic noise and 94.4 ± 1.9% under human annotation noise. Contributions measure gradient-scatter deletion without retraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mislabeled examples disproportionately contribute to Fisher effective-rank expansion during memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: Rank onset precedes test degradation across the convolutional threshold grid, whereas ViT mean lead times range from −7 to 22 epochs depending on thresholds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retrospective Fisher-rank onset can precede test degradation, with architecture- and threshold-dependent timing.

record.problems: Clean test-accuracy trajectories are described but numerical values are not stated in the supplied text. The training and evaluation subsets are sampled subsets; several timing conclusions use retrospective thresholds, and the authors describe lead time as threshold-dependent for the Vision Transformer.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the clean test-accuracy outcomes under partial label corruption do not measure the specific random-label versus natural-label comparison in V1; the other versions' named interventions or measurements are not tested.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting and above-chance natural-label generalization under the same recipe, with chance-level held-out accuracy under random labels. Partial corruption and near-perfect training accuracy alone do not establish this comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under comparable tuning. Different optimizers are used for different architectures without a controlled optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects and recipe adaptations under fixed epoch budgets; all experiments use batch size 128.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence, retraining, and comparing test accuracy with matched random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. No rows require correction, and no omitted result warrants a V1–V8 verdict. The accuracy trajectories were already declared in rows_left_out. The study cites the original V1 and V8 sources, but its own spectral measurements do not test those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests symmetric partial label corruption and clean test performance, not fitting fixed random labels alongside natural labels under the same recipe, nor whether held-out accuracy remains far above chance.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples, retraining, and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
